title: Near-real-time consumer activity weakens while entertainment spending and payment failures diverge
source_unit: Office for National Statistics Economic activity and social change in the UK, real-time indicators: 17 September 2026
geography: United Kingdom, with regional retail-footfall comparisons and UK-wide aggregated payment indicators

observations.period: August 2026 compared with July 2026 and August 2025; retail footfall and card spending

denominator.unit: experimental index and aggregated card-spending comparison; no unique-person denominator

retail_footfall_month_on_month.unit: percent change in estimated UK retail footfall from July 2026

retail_footfall_year_on_year.unit: percent change in estimated UK retail footfall from August 2025

revolut_debit_spending_month_on_month.unit: percent change in seasonally adjusted Revolut debit-card spending from July 2026

revolut_debit_spending_year_on_year.unit: percent change in seasonally adjusted Revolut debit-card spending from August 2025

entertainment_spending_year_on_year.unit: percent change in Revolut debit-card entertainment spending from August 2025

mechanism.value: Aggregate consumer activity can soften month-on-month while selected discretionary categories, including entertainment, remain above the prior year; footfall, payment value, and category spending are separate behavioral stages

observations.method: ONS real-time indicators using BT Active Intelligence estimated retail footfall and anonymised aggregated Revolut debit-card spending; the bulletin reports month-on-month and year-on-year changes.
observations.uncertainty: These are official statistics in development. Footfall counts visits rather than unique people, excludes people who live and work in retail areas, and is not seasonally adjusted; Revolut spending is a participating-card sample and current-price transaction value, not household welfare or total UK spending.
observations.subgroup: Visitors to UK retail locations and Revolut debit-card transactions represented in the aggregated indicator, with category and regional breakdowns where available.
observations.counterinterpretation: Calendar effects, inflation, sample composition, tourism, and changes in payment method can explain divergence; higher entertainment card spending does not establish higher attendance, affordability, or cultural satisfaction.

observations.period: August 2026 compared with August 2025; direct-debit payment reliability

denominator.unit: sample of anonymised and aggregated Bacs Direct Debit payments; no unique-household denominator

direct_debit_failure_rate_2025.unit: percent of sampled Direct Debit payments failing in August 2025

direct_debit_failure_rate_2026.unit: percent of sampled Direct Debit payments failing in August 2026

failure_rate_change.unit: percentage-point increase in the sampled Direct Debit failure rate

category_signal.value: Fitness-facility failure rates rose from 5.7% to 6.1%, while loan failure rates rose from 4.7% to 5.0%

mechanism.value: Payment failure can reveal household budget friction at recurring commitments, with discretionary fitness and loan categories showing higher failure rates than the aggregate series

observations.method: ONS real-time indicator based on seasonally adjusted Direct Debit average transaction and failure-rate data supplied by Pay.UK and Vocalink.
observations.uncertainty: The data are anonymised and aggregated, the underlying rates are low and volatile, and failure does not identify the reason, household, later recovery, cancellation, arrears, or harm.
observations.subgroup: Sampled Bacs Direct Debit payments by selected payment category.
observations.counterinterpretation: A failed payment can reflect an account change, technical issue, timing, merchant retry, or intentional cancellation rather than financial distress; category rates are not population prevalence.

observations.period: August 2026 compared with July 2026 and August 2025; automotive fuel demand

denominator.unit: average fuel quantity demanded per aggregated card transaction; no household denominator

fuel_price_growth_change_month_on_month.unit: percentage-point increase in the growth rate of average automotive fuel prices from July 2026

fuel_quantity_demand_growth_change_month.unit: percentage-point change in growth of average quantity demanded per fuel transaction from July 2026

fuel_quantity_demand_growth_change_year_.unit: percentage-point change in growth of average quantity demanded per fuel transaction from August 2025

mechanism.value: Price pressure can appear as lower quantity demanded per fuel transaction, adding a mobility-cost channel to consumer and cultural optionality without observing individual travel decisions

observations.method: ONS real-time indicator combining aggregated anonymised card-spending data with Department for Energy Security and Net Zero road-fuel price, sales, and stock data.
observations.uncertainty: The indicator is aggregated and current-price oriented; it does not identify drivers, trip purpose, fuel substitution, mileage, income, or whether reduced quantity reflects fewer trips or different refuelling timing.
observations.subgroup: Aggregated UK automotive-fuel transactions represented in the indicator.
observations.counterinterpretation: Fuel demand per transaction can change because of tank size, refuelling timing, vehicle mix, travel seasonality, or price promotions rather than a general reduction in mobility.

related_sources.claim: ONS landing page for the real-time indicators bulletin, release date, headline consumer findings, and official-statistics-in-development designation.
ONS HTML bulletin with consumer behaviour, footfall, Revolut spending, Direct Debit failure, fuel demand, data-source, and limitation statements.

boundary: This record adds a near-real-time UK consumer and payment-friction layer. It does not establish household-level financial distress, total consumer spending, cultural attendance, mobility reduction, causal price effects, or later remedy and trust outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official ONS 17 September 2026 real-time-indicators PDF reviewed for August retail footfall, Revolut spending, Direct Debit failure rates, fuel prices and demand, source construction, and official-statistics-in-development limitations.
